name: Priligy (dapoxetine)
summary: Medicine taken as needed by adult men to help delay ejaculation and improve control during sex. It works on serotonin in the brain, taken 1–3 hours before sexual activity.
description: Priligy contains dapoxetine, a short-acting selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) used for premature ejaculation in adult men between 18 and 64 years old. It helps increase the time to ejaculation, improve control, and reduce distress. It is only taken when needed and not every day. Some men may feel dizzy, light-headed, or faint, especially when first using it or when standing up quickly.
patient_summary: Priligy is used to treat premature ejaculation in men. You take it only when you need it, about 1 to 3 hours before sex. It can help you last longer and feel more in control. A common problem is feeling dizzy or faint, especially when you stand up. Taking it with a full glass of water and avoiding alcohol can help. Do not take more than one pill in 24 hours.

linked_conditions.context: Used to increase time to ejaculation and improve control during sexual activity.

contraindications: Using MAOIs or within 14 days of using them
Taking other SSRIs/SNRIs/TCAs or certain depression medicines
Taking certain antifungal or HIV medicines
History of mania or severe depression
Serious heart problems or heart rhythm disorders
History of fainting or low blood pressure episodes

pharmacokinetics.duration_IR: Short-acting; taken only before sexual activity

sections.heading: What is Priligy used for?
sections.text: Priligy is used to treat premature ejaculation in adult men aged 18–64 who usually ejaculate within about 2 minutes and feel distress or relationship difficulty because of it. It can help you last longer and feel more control.

quotes: Taken when you need it, not every day.
Some men feel faint or dizzy, especially when standing

sections.heading: How long does it take to work?
key_points: Effect lasts for the sexual event
Not meant for daily continuous use

sections.heading: Important Safety Information
sections.highlight: Priligy can make you faint. If you feel faint, dizzy, or light-headed, lie down or sit with your head between your knees until you feel better.
sections.black_box: Do NOT take more than one tablet in 24 hours due to increased risk of fainting or low blood pressure.
other: Avoid alcohol (higher risk of dizziness or fainting)
Tell your doctor if you have thoughts of harming yourself
Do not use with certain depression medicines, MAOIs, antifungals, or HIV medicines
Your doctor may check your blood pressure while standing
patient_counseling: Always take with a full glass of water
Do not stand up too quickly
Stop and seek help if you faint

common.patient_note: Stand up slowly, drink water, lie down if needed.
Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.

items.action: Avoid and wait the recommended time
Do not combine unless directed by your doctor

sections.heading: Stopping Priligy
sections.text: Priligy is taken only when needed, not daily, so there is no typical withdrawal. Some men may briefly notice dizziness or sleep problems after stopping. Speak with your doctor if this happens.

sections.heading: How to take it
sections.text: Priligy is taken only when needed before sexual activity.

adult.max: Do not take more than one tablet in 24 hours
adult.with_water: Take with at least one full glass of water
adult.avoid: Avoid alcohol and grapefruit juice within 24 hours

sections.simple_explanation: Most men take 30 mg about 1–3 hours before sex, with water, and no more than once a day.

sections.heading: Who should NOT take it
sections.text: Priligy is only for adult men 18–64.
sections.hepatic: Avoid if moderate or severe liver problems
sections.renal: Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease

sections.heading: What it looks like
sections.text: Film-coated tablets, usually 30 mg. Check your package for the exact strength.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Priligy briefly increases serotonin activity in the brain, which can delay ejaculation and improve control during sex.

sections.heading: Practical use
sections.text: Used when needed, especially when premature ejaculation causes distress or affects relationships. Can be an option if other non-medicine approaches have not been enough.
